title: Peer validation workflow and corpus-provenance crosswalk
scope: Inspect an open-source DWG/DXF project's actual contributor validation workflow, beyond headline format support.
Distinguish fast tests, corpus diffs, mixed-toolchain conversion/reopen, and fuzz/sanitizer campaigns.
Refine the existing plan's evidence ladder and external self-unblocking behavior without adding routine expensive tests.

sources.revision: Mutable upstream master documentation and scripts inspected 2026-10-20; no source commit or executable was pinned or run.
sources.observed: Contributor guidance prefers make check for normal changes and describes ASan as slow, with ODA File Converter audit/round-trip checks as a separate interoperability route. test-dxf.sh normalizes generated output and compares it to expected DXF when available. dxf-roundtrip.sh composes LibreDWG DWG-to-DXF, ODA File Converter DXF-to-DWG, and dwgread reopen. The manual explicitly enumerates families lacking test coverage; HACKING describes fuzz workflows and the need for DWG/DXF pairs when reverse-engineering unknown layouts.
sources.limits: These are process and coverage disclosures, not results for libdxfrw, normative format rules, or proof that a particular LibreDWG release passes each route. The converter round-trip is mixed-toolchain evidence and must be reported by stage. No peer binary, ODA converter, corpus drawing, or fuzz campaign was run.

sources.revision: Shared worktree plan inspected and updated 2026-10-20.
sources.observed: The plan already requires focused generated fast tests, rare composed peer/native checks, no imported external fixtures, and a self-unblocking implementation queue. This pass makes those practices an explicit evidence ladder and clarifies that synthetic vectors cannot establish unknown producer semantics.
sources.limits: The update adds no local behavior, feature finding, test, fixture, dependency, or support evidence. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain external-only and non-promoting.

existingSubplansRefined: PAR-06: distinguish class/opaque pass-through from tested semantic support and preserve test-coverage gaps explicitly.
PAR-07/S8: separate local generated vectors, producer-pair differential, mixed-toolchain round-trip stages, strict reopen, and consumer acceptance.
PAR-14: keep fast leaf validation separate from low-frequency fuzz/sanitizer campaigns, triggered by relevant parser-safety changes or scheduled integration checkpoints.
Implementation process: after each item update status/evidence and self-unblock to the next local task; unavailable external evidence defers only its claim.
